description: Create 1 to 100 monitors in one call, all or nothing; for a single monitor use create_monitor. Requires a key with the write scope. An invalid item, or a batch that would exceed the plan, rejects the whole call and creates nothing: call get_plan_usage first to check the batch fits. Errors name the failing item. A field that fails validation is named by its path, such as monitors.3.target (index 3 is the fourth item; all such errors are reported at once). Any other item error keeps the status create_monitor would give (403 when its interval or regions break the plan or name an unknown region, 404 for an unknown channel id, 422 for its config or its type's region rules) and its reason starts with monitors[3] ("<item name>"): — only the first such item is reported. Read the index only from that leading monitors[N] (the pattern ^monitors\[(\d+)\] after any lead-in such as "Forbidden: " or "Invalid request: "), never from the name, which may itself contain quotes or brackets. A plan-limit 403 without that prefix is about the batch as a whole: together the items would exceed the plan's monitor count or its quota of monitors below 60 seconds. Fix the item or shrink the batch and send the whole call again. Returns monitors: one list_monitors row per created monitor, in request order. The example is a port-list TCP monitor, which takes exactly one region and an interval of at least 300 seconds. Example: {"monitors": [{"name": "db.example.com exposed ports", "type": "TCP", "target": "db.example.com", "interval_seconds": 3600, "timeout_seconds": 10, "regions": ["eu-central"], "config": {"ports": [5432, 6379, 27017], "expected_state": "closed"}}]}

monitors.description: 1 to 100 monitors, each taking the same fields and rules as create_monitor's arguments. Items with is_active false are created paused and still count toward the plan. Unless the user names regions, give each item every code in limits.allowed_regions, up to the plan's max_regions; tell the user the intervals you chose.

name: bulk_create_monitors

status.description: Known values: PENDING, UP, DEGRADED, DOWN, PAUSED.

type.description: Known values: HTTP, PING, SSL, TCP, DNS.
